issues.detail: The Greek 'εαν υμων πρωτον απο μερους εμπλησθω' uses the verb 'εμπλησθω' (from πληρόω), which means to be filled, satisfied, or fulfilled. The Vietnamese translation 'thỏa lòng một phần' (satisfied a part/portion) slightly misses the nuance of being 'filled/fulfilled' in the context of completion of the ministry, but more importantly, the Greek structure suggests a condition: 'if I may first be filled/satisfied by you'. The Vietnamese 'sau khi' (after) changes the temporal relationship from a conditional 'if' (εαν) to a sequential 'after'.
